clockReferenceDateTime.description: Clock Reference to be used to record time.  This allows the application to synchronize its time with that of the server.  Data Representation Temporal Data Element Specification following ISO-8601:2000 specification.  The granularity for date-time for this API will always be the following: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss-+hh:mm.  where -+ is either minus or plus depending on whether the offset from GMT is positive or negative hours minute.

singlePolicyRequestIndicator.description: True indicates that the user may select only 1 policy per request.  They may have multiple entries each with a different earning type.  Once the first entry is made, the policy is frozen for that request.

balancesIndicator.description: True indicates that the system manages balances for the user.  The balances may be zero.  If true the application will show the balances screen.

requestsIndicator.description: True indicates that the system manages requests for the user.  It is possible that the user has no requests.  e.g. A new hire which has not submitted any requests for time off yet, but may.

paidTimeOffPolicies.description: A list of paid time off policies and their characteristics.  A client defines which earning type codes go with the policy, the default quantity of time to take, and whether it is taken by days or hours.  For example, an employer may create a Half Vacation Day Policy.  This would have an earningsCode of Vacation and the default quantity of 4 hours.  The user only needs to enter the day.

paidTimeOffPolicy.description: code identifying the time off policy.  A system may have 1 policy per earning type.  If there earning type has only 1 earning type then the paidTimeOffPolicycode should be equal to the earningTypeCode. If there is a policy with multiple earning Types then the user must first select the policy.  If there are multiple possible earning types then the user is presented with the list to select from.  The list is presented in the order which it is sent in the JSON.  The first one is the default presented.

labelName.description: The label which will be shown in the UI for the policy.

defaultQuantity.description: For the request type a default quantity of hours or days may be defined.  The user may override this.

valueNumber.description: A positive or negative number indicating the quantity.  +-99999.99999  The application will truncate the decimal places if it can not fit on the screen.

unitTimeCode.description: The units in which the quantity is communicated.

defaultTime.description: The default time used for a duration entry where the durationPrecision is hh:mm

defaultStartTime.description: For an entry type which has time this will be the default start time shown to the user.  The user may change this. This is communicated in military time.  The application converts it for display purposes based on the timeNotationCode.

defaultEndTime.description: For an entry type which has time this will be the default end time shown to the user.  The user may change this. This is communicated in military time.  The application converts it for display purposes based on the timeNotationCode.  17:00 will show as 5:00 pm if the timeNotationCode is 12h

entryTypeCodes.description: A list of  types of entries supported for the entry type.  An earning type may be entered in varying ways depending on whether it is a single day or a period. dateDuration represents a date and number of hours.  timePeriod represents a startDateTime and endDateTime.  endDateTime is optional.  datePeriod represents a startDate and an endDate.  The endDate is optional. dateTime represents a date with optional time.  A date alone indicates a full day.  A dateTime can also be a date with a start time and an end time.  There may be a combination of types in the case where one rule applies for a single day or a time period. datePeriodHalfDay indicates that a half day is taken each day in the specified period.  The System of Record calculates what is considered a half day for the worker.

partialDayIndicator.description: True indicates that this entry type allows partial day to be entered.  Example 2 hours.  This will trigger the UI to allow a time to be entered in a time off request.  False will only allow full days to be entered.

minimumQuantity.description: The minimum amount of time which can be requested.  Example 4 hours or 1 day

minimumIncrement.description: The minimum increment of time which can be requested.  For example,  30 minute is the minimum increment.  Therefore, I can not request 4 hours and 30 minute, but I can not request 4 hours and 45 minute.

The lexical representation of a time zone is a string of the form: (('+' | '-') hh ':' mm) | 'Z', where hh is a two-digit numeral (with leading zeros as required) that represents the hours, mm is a two-digit numeral that represents the minute, '+' indicates a nonnegative duration, '-' indicates a non-positive duration. 'Z' indicates the UTC time zone

links.description: A link description object is used to describe link relations.  In the context of a schema, it defines the link relations of the instances of the schema, and can be parameterized by the instance values.  The link description format can be used on its own in regular (non-schema documents), and use of this format can be declared by referencing the normative link description schema as the the schema for the data structure that uses the links.

rel.description: Indicates the nature of the relationship of the related resource to the resource that generated this representation

href.description: The value of the href link description property is a template used to determine the target URI of the related resource.  The value of the instance property SHOULD be resolved as a URI-Reference per RFC 3986 [RFC3986] and MAY be a relative reference to a URI.

method.description: The HTTP method to use to traverse the link (GET, POST, PUT or DELETE).

mediaType.description: The media type that the linked resource will return (Response)

encType.description: If present, this property indicates a query media type format that the server supports for querying or posting to the collection of instances at the target resource.  The query can be suffixed to the target URI to query the collection with property-based constraints on the resources that SHOULD be returned from the server or used to post data to the resource (depending on the method). (Request)

schema.description: This property contains a schema which defines the acceptable structure of the submitted request.  For a GET request, this schema would define the properties for the query string and for a POST request, this would define the body.

targetSchema.description: This property is a schema that defines the expected structure of the JSON representation of the target of the link, if the target of the link is returned using JSON representation.

title.description: This property defines a title for the link.  The value must be a string. User agents MAY use this title when presenting the link to the user.

arguments.description: A map that may be used as the basis for any data (arguments or properties) required to follow the link.
